ComposeCodingRules.Mission:
Baseline rules for writing Jetpack Compose UI code (`@Composable` functions, `Modifier` chains, side-effect entry points, state management, previews). Layered on top of `kotlin-rules` and `kotlin-coroutines` — inherits the KDoc contract, structural anchors, null-safety, immutability, and structured-concurrency axioms; adds Compose-specific enforcement.
Scope: Compose UI (`androidx.compose.ui`), Compose Runtime (`androidx.compose.runtime`), Compose Foundation (`androidx.compose.foundation`), Material (M2 / M3), Compose lifecycle interop (`collectAsStateWithLifecycle`), Compose testing (`androidx.compose.ui.test`). Not scoped: Compose Multiplatform desktop / iOS specifics, Compose for Wear OS, Compose-based navigation libraries (Navigation-Compose is layered on top when in use — treat as project-level directive).
Sources (public standards): official Compose docs (developer.android.com/jetpack/compose), Compose API guidelines (android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main/compose/docs/compose-api-guidelines.md), Compose lifecycle & side-effects guide, Compose performance guide (stability, `derivedStateOf`, `key`, `remember`), «Thinking in Compose» talk series. Adopted as timeless engineering practice; version numbers and coordinates omitted.
**Base axiom:** a `@Composable` function is not a regular function. It runs an unknown number of times, on an unknown thread schedule chosen by the runtime, and it must be **restartable, skippable, and idempotent** with respect to its parameters. Every rule below closes one of those three guarantees.
**Position in the rules cascade:** `kotlin-rules` (language) → `kotlin-coroutines` (concurrency) → `compose-rules` (UI framework). A composable file activates all three; a non-composable Kotlin file only activates the first two.

BeliefState.Axiom: A `@Composable` function's body MUST be deterministic in its parameters and its `remember`-scoped state. No hidden mutable reads (mutable globals, `Date()`, `Random.nextX()` outside `remember`), no direct `withContext` / `runBlocking` (composables cannot suspend into I/O directly — that belongs to a side-effect entry point per `AX_SIDE_EFFECTS`). - Non-deterministic sources (`Random`, current time, generated ids) go into a `remember { ... }` block so the value is stable across recompositions and captured once per composition. - Composables MUST NOT write to `mutableStateOf(...)` during composition — the write is either dropped (`remember` runs once) or triggers an infinite recomposition loop. Writes belong to callbacks (`onClick = { count.value++ }`) or side-effects (`LaunchedEffect`). - I/O, disk reads, blocking calls in a composable body are forbidden — they run on the UI thread every recomposition. Move them to `LaunchedEffect`, `produceState`, or (better) upstream `ViewModel`.

State ownership follows the hoisting principle: the composable that OBSERVES state and the composable that MUTATES state may differ, but the state itself lives at the LOWEST common ancestor that needs both. Rules: - A composable with mutating callbacks MUST be «stateless» — accept `value: T` and `onValueChange: (T) -> Unit` (or the same pair with domain-specific names). Never own `mutableStateOf(...)` inside a reusable UI component. - «Stateful» wrappers exist for convenience only: they hold the `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` and delegate to the stateless variant. The stateful variant is a thin convenience — NEVER the primary export in a design-system library. - Screen-level state (form data, page filter, selection) lives in `ViewModel` and reaches the screen as a `StateFlow` collected via `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` per `kotlin-coroutines` `AX_FLOW_DISCIPLINE`. Composables never talk to a repository directly. - `MutableState<T>` (from `mutableStateOf`) is Compose's snapshot-observable box; it MUST be wrapped in `remember { }` at its point of creation, otherwise every recomposition creates a new box and every write is lost.

`remember { ... }` is the composable-scoped memoization primitive. Rules: - Any expensive computation, any object with an identity that must survive recompositions, and any `MutableState` MUST live inside `remember`. Un-remembered objects are recreated every recomposition. - `remember(key1, key2, ...) { ... }` invalidates the memo when a key changes. Use keys derived from the semantic identity of the value — never `Unit` (a static memo is `remember { ... }` without keys) and never a mutable reference (memo would recompute on every recomposition). - `rememberSaveable { ... }` persists across process death via `SavedInstanceState`. Use for UI-state that MUST survive Activity recreation (form input, scroll position for a manually-managed list, expansion flags) — NOT for domain data (that belongs to `ViewModel` + `SavedStateHandle`). - `remember { mutableStateOf(x) }` is the canonical local-state pattern; the shorter `by remember { mutableStateOf(x) }` (property delegate) is preferred at declaration sites for readability. - `derivedStateOf { ... }` wraps a computation that reads other snapshot state and MUST recompute only when its dependencies change — cheap enough to be recomputed lazily, but reads should trigger recomposition of consumers only when the DERIVED value changes. Wrong use (`derivedStateOf` around a non-snapshot read) is a silent no-op.

Every action that observes the world outside composition (network call, coroutine launch, subscription, callback registration, resource acquisition) MUST enter through a Compose-runtime side-effect entry. Enforced matrix:
| Effect API | Runs when | Cancelled when | Use for | |---|---|---|---| | `LaunchedEffect(key1, ...) { ... }` | keys enter composition or change | keys change or composable leaves composition | suspend work bound to composition scope (fetch on first display, restart when `id` changes) | | `DisposableEffect(key1, ...) { ...; onDispose { ... } }` | keys enter composition or change | keys change or composable leaves composition | subscribe/unsubscribe pairs (register + `onDispose { unregister }`) | | `SideEffect { ... }` | every successful composition | never (side channel) | publish snapshot state to non-Compose observers (analytics event on state change); NOT for I/O | | `rememberCoroutineScope()` | first composition; scope survives composition | composable leaves composition | coroutine started FROM a user callback (button click launches a suspend) — never from composition itself | | `produceState(initial, key1, ...) { ... }` | keys enter / change | keys change or composable leaves composition | one-shot suspend that yields a `State<T>` (initial value + subsequent emissions via `value = ...`) | | `snapshotFlow { ... }` | collector active | collector cancelled | convert snapshot reads (Compose state) to a cold `Flow` (rare — usually last resort) |
Rules: - The keys passed to `LaunchedEffect` / `DisposableEffect` / `produceState` ARE the restart contract. Missing keys = «run once», keys = «restart on change». `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` runs once on enter and cancels on leave — the correct form for «init on show, cleanup on hide». - NEVER call `viewModelScope.launch` / a service's own scope from inside composition. Launching from composition ties the coroutine to a lifecycle Compose does not own — a rotation or navigation-away leaks or double-launches. - `rememberCoroutineScope()` gives a scope tied to the composition entry point; use it ONLY from user-triggered callbacks, never from composition body directly (composition body has no user intent). - `SideEffect` runs on the main thread every successful composition — it is cheap only for pure snapshot-→non-compose bridges. I/O inside `SideEffect` blocks the UI thread every frame the composition succeeds.

Compose skips recomposition of a composable when ALL of its parameters are equal to the previous invocation (structural equality). Skipping requires ALL parameters to be of **stable** types. Rules: - Data classes with only `val`s of stable types are stable if the compiler-plugin can prove immutability. Mark opinionated stability with `@Immutable` (fields are conceptually immutable, `equals` is meaningful) or `@Stable` (public reads are safe to observe, mutations notify consumers — used for observable holders). - Public `List` / `Set` / `Map` are **unstable by default** (the runtime cannot prove the underlying map isn't `MutableMap`). Use `kotlinx.collections.immutable.ImmutableList` / `PersistentList` or wrap collections in an `@Immutable` holder to restore skippability. Plain `listOf(...)` is fine at call sites (compiler proves via allocation site); a `List` parameter received from outside is not. - `lambda` parameters that close over unstable state (or capture composition-local `remember` values without keys) prevent skipping. Extract lambda parameters into `remember { ... }` if they are hot recomposition offenders. - Read Compose Compiler reports (`composeCompiler.reportsDestination = ...`) to identify unstable parameters before optimising blindly — most «recomposes too much» findings surface there. - `@Immutable` / `@Stable` are contracts to the compiler — misapplying them (marking a class with `var` fields as `@Immutable`) silently breaks recomposition; the compiler trusts the annotation.

`Modifier` is order-sensitive and MUST be the LAST parameter of every non-terminal `@Composable` with a visual role. Rules: - Every reusable composable accepts `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` as the LAST parameter. Callers pass position / sizing / semantics via the modifier — the composable NEVER hard-codes `Modifier.padding(16.dp)` on its own root. The composable is a shape; the modifier is placement. - Order matters: `Modifier.padding(8.dp).background(Color.Red)` differs from `Modifier.background(Color.Red).padding(8.dp)` (former: padding around a red box; latter: red padded box). Every ordering choice in a composable body MUST be intentional; document non-obvious orderings in an inline comment. - `Modifier.composed { ... }` is the ONLY way to build a modifier that itself uses `remember` / composition-locals. A modifier factory that does `Modifier.something(remember { ... })` breaks composition rules — the `remember` runs outside a composable and throws. - `Modifier` allocations at call sites are cheap in Compose Compiler ≥1.5 (memoized by the plugin); do not pre-hoist `Modifier` chains into `remember` blocks unless a profiler says otherwise.

`@Composable` functions that emit UI use `PascalCase` (`OrderList`, `PriceCard`) — they are noun-shaped surfaces, not verbs, per official Compose API guidelines. `@Composable` functions that return a value (do NOT emit) follow the regular Kotlin verb convention (`rememberScrollState`, `animateColorAsState`). - Never prefix with `Show*` / `Draw*` — the noun is the surface. A `Show` verb belongs to a state-management API, not a rendering function. - Slot parameters (`content: @Composable () -> Unit`) are named after the slot's role (`title`, `actions`, `content`) — never `slot1` / `bodyLambda`. - Suffix `*Preview` reserved for `@Preview`-annotated helpers (`OrderListPreview_Loaded`, `OrderListPreview_Empty`). Preview names document the scenario in the name.

Every reusable composable in a design-system or shared UI module has `@Preview` coverage across the meaningful state axes. Rules: - One `@Preview` per distinct visual state (loaded, empty, error, loading, RTL, dark theme, large font). Multi-state coverage is not a Storybook «nice-to-have» — a missing state is an untested render. - Previews MUST NOT touch real dependencies (no `hiltViewModel()` in a preview, no `LocalContext.current.getSystemService(...)` with side effects). Fake dependencies via preview-parameter providers or local test doubles. - `@PreviewParameter(...)` is the canonical way to sweep parametric state (list of sample orders → one preview per sample); avoid hand-rolled preview loops. - Preview functions are `private` and named `Preview_` for grep-navigation. - Do NOT wrap production `LaunchedEffect` / real network in a `@Preview` composable — preview runs in the IDE / release APK; a fetch in preview leaks credentials and crashes without emulator context. If a composable requires an effect to render sensibly, provide a preview-only variant that injects a fake state.

`CompositionLocal` is the last-resort dependency-injection mechanism in Compose — implicit, un-typed by the composable signature, and easy to misuse. Rules: - Use `CompositionLocal` only for cross-cutting UI-only dependencies (theme, typography, `LocalContentColor`, `LocalDensity`); never for domain services (repositories, use-cases). Domain services enter via `ViewModel` or explicit parameters. - Define via `compositionLocalOf { defaultValue }` (recomposes readers on change) or `staticCompositionLocalOf { ... }` (does NOT recompose — for values that never change during composition, e.g. `LocalDensity`). Wrong choice: `compositionLocalOf` for a static value burns recompositions; `staticCompositionLocalOf` for a changing value silently keeps stale readers. - Provide via `CompositionLocalProvider(LocalX provides value) { content() }` at the module root, never scattered mid-tree unless the intent is to override for a subtree. - Every custom `CompositionLocal` MUST have a `@Composable`-agnostic default (`error("Local not provided")` in `staticCompositionLocalOf { ... }` when a provider is mandatory).

`LazyColumn` / `LazyRow` / `LazyVerticalGrid` items MUST supply a `key` when the collection can reorder, insert, or remove — otherwise Compose maps by position and stateful children (animations, `remember`-holdings, focus) attach to the wrong item. Rules: - `items(list, key = { it.id }) { ... }` is the canonical form. Missing `key` is a bug on any list with reordering / removal. - `contentType` is the second parameter — supply when the list is heterogeneous so Compose can reuse layouts across types. - `key` MUST be stable and unique per item (typically the domain id). NEVER use `hashCode()` of a mutable object or the item's index (defeats the purpose).

Compose UI is tested via `androidx.compose.ui.test` (`ComposeTestRule`, `createComposeRule` / `createAndroidComposeRule`, `onNodeWithTag` / `onNodeWithText`, `performClick`, `assertIsDisplayed`). Rules: - Prefer semantics-based queries (`onNodeWithContentDescription`, `onNodeWithText`) over `onNodeWithTag` — mirrors accessibility semantics and reveals a11y regressions. - `Modifier.testTag(...)` is used ONLY when semantic queries are insufficient (rare: layout containers with no text / no content description). - Time is virtual by default via `mainClock` — `mainClock.advanceTimeBy(1000)` advances animations without wall-clock delay. - Isolate coroutine dispatchers per `kotlin-coroutines` `AX_COROUTINE_TESTING` — the test rule integrates with the composition dispatcher; but any `viewModel` under test uses an injected `TestDispatcher`, not a hard-coded one.

Definitions.Definition: A composable that takes `value` + `onValueChange` (or the domain analogue) and owns no `MutableState`. Reusable, testable in isolation, and portable across screens.
A thin convenience wrapper around a stateless composable: holds `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` and forwards `value` / `onValueChange` to the stateless variant. Never the primary export.
A composable that can be re-executed by the runtime with the same parameters and produce identical UI. Enforced by `AX_COMPOSABLE_PURITY`.
A composable whose recomposition can be skipped when ALL parameters are equal-by-structure to the previous call. Requires stable parameters per `AX_STABILITY_AND_SKIPPING`.
One of `LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect`, `SideEffect`, `rememberCoroutineScope`, `produceState`, `snapshotFlow`. The ONLY sanctioned entries into non-composition work.

Pattern.Intent: State-hoisted counter: stateless variant is the reusable primitive; a thin `rememberCounter` / stateful wrapper exists for convenience only.
Pattern.Why: Stateless variant is testable in isolation and reusable in every screen. Stateful wrapper exists purely as a code-golf convenience; libraries export the stateless form as the primary API per `AX_STATE_HOISTING`.

Pattern.Intent: Restart a fetch when `orderId` changes; cancel automatically when the composable leaves.
Pattern.Why: `LaunchedEffect(orderId)` restarts on id change and cancels on leave — the restart contract is the key. `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` would run once and never restart. `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` respects Android lifecycle per `kotlin-coroutines` `AX_FLOW_DISCIPLINE`.

Pattern.Intent: Subscribe / unsubscribe pair anchored to composition lifetime — analytics screen-view event.
Pattern.Why: `DisposableEffect` binds the subscribe/unsubscribe pair to composition lifetime. `LaunchedEffect` would need a `try { … } finally { … }` pattern with weaker guarantees (finally runs on cancellation but not on structural re-key without cleanup).

Pattern.Intent: Coroutine launched from a user callback — `rememberCoroutineScope` is the correct scope entry.
Pattern.Why: The suspend call belongs to a user event, not to composition itself. `rememberCoroutineScope` scope survives recompositions; leaves composition = scope cancelled. Direct `LaunchedEffect` here would fire on every composition, not on click.

Pattern.Intent: Restore skippability for a composable receiving a list from outside — `ImmutableList` marks the boundary.
Pattern.Why: Plain `List<Order>` parameter is unstable — the runtime cannot prove the underlying map isn't `MutableList`. `ImmutableList` (or an `@Immutable`-annotated holder) restores skipping. `items(key = { ... })` is required per `AX_LAZY_LIST_KEYS`.

Pattern.Intent: `derivedStateOf` caches a computed value; consumers recompose only when the derived value changes, not when its inputs change.
Pattern.Why: `listState.firstVisibleItemIndex` changes on every scroll pixel; a bare read would recompose the FAB on every frame. `derivedStateOf` recomputes but only invalidates readers when the boolean actually flips — one recomposition at the threshold crossing, not thousands.

Pattern.Intent: `ViewModel` exposes `StateFlow`; UI collects with lifecycle awareness.
Pattern.Why: `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` respects `Lifecycle.State.STARTED` — the UI pauses collection when backgrounded, avoiding wasted emissions and battery. `by` delegate makes the state read syntactically identical to a property access. `when` on a sealed `OrdersState` gives exhaustive rendering per `kotlin-rules` `AX_WHEN_EXHAUSTIVENESS`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun Bad() { var x by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }; x++; Text("$x") }` — mutation inside composition body triggers infinite recomposition.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Every write invalidates the composable → re-runs → writes again → infinite loop. Violates `AX_COMPOSABLE_PURITY`. Writes belong to callbacks or side-effect entries.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun Bad() { var x by mutableStateOf(0); Button(onClick = { x++ }) { Text("$x") } }` — missing `remember` around `mutableStateOf`.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: `mutableStateOf(0)` allocates a NEW `MutableState` every recomposition, so every button press resets to 0. Violates `AX_REMEMBER_DISCIPLINE`.
AntiPattern.Good: ```kotlin var x by remember { mutableStateOf(0) } // one box, survives recompositions ```

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun Bad(vm: VM) { vm.scope.launch { vm.load() }; Text("...") }` — launching from composition body.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: The launch fires on every recomposition (potentially many times per second), leaks / double-fetches, and ties the coroutine to a scope Compose does not own. Violates `AX_SIDE_EFFECTS`.
AntiPattern.Good: ```kotlin LaunchedEffect(Unit) { vm.load() } // fires once on enter, cancels on leave ```

AntiPattern.Bad: `items(orders) { OrderRow(it) }` — no `key` on a reorderable list.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Compose maps items by index. Insertion / reorder attaches state (animations, expansion, focus, `rememberSaveable`) to the wrong item. Visual jank + wrong state. Violates `AX_LAZY_LIST_KEYS`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun MyCard(text: String) { Card(modifier = Modifier.padding(16.dp)) { Text(text) } }` — the composable owns its outer padding.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: The composable now has a hidden opinion about its container's spacing. Every caller inherits the padding and cannot remove it. Violates `AX_MODIFIER_CHAIN`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun BadList(items: List<Order>) { ... }` — plain `List` parameter breaks skipping.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: The Compose Compiler cannot prove `List` is immutable; the composable becomes non-skippable and re-runs on every parent recomposition. Violates `AX_STABILITY_AND_SKIPPING`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `val LocalOrdersRepo = compositionLocalOf<OrdersRepo> { error("no repo") }` — domain service in a `CompositionLocal`.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Implicit dependency invisible in composable signature; testability collapses (every test must wrap in `CompositionLocalProvider`); coupling between UI and repository grows sideways. Violates `AX_COMPOSITION_LOCAL_DISCIPLINE`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Preview @Composable fun MyPreview() { OrdersScreen(hiltViewModel()) }` — preview instantiates a real Hilt ViewModel.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Preview runs outside Application context; `hiltViewModel()` throws or fetches real data / credentials. Preview becomes non-functional and the failure mode is silent (broken preview panel). Violates `AX_PREVIEW_DISCIPLINE`.

AntiPattern.Bad: `@Composable fun Bad() { val json = File("cfg.json").readText(); Text(json) }` — I/O on the UI thread every recomposition.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Runs on the main thread on every composition. Violates `AX_COMPOSABLE_PURITY`; jank at best, ANR at worst.

Hook.Purpose: Compose compiler runs during Kotlin compilation; verifies annotations, checks `@Composable` call sites, emits stability reports.
Hook.Expected: Exit 0. Compose Compiler warnings on `@Composable` misuse elevated to error via compiler flags where project standards demand.

Hook.Purpose: Compose Compiler emits per-composable stability reports (`composables.txt`, `classes.txt`) when configured; used to audit skippability.
Hook.Expected: `build/compose_compiler/*.txt` produced. Composables marked `restartable skippable` where inputs are stable; any `restartable !skippable` finding traced to an unstable parameter (usually a raw `List` / lambda capture).

Hook.Purpose: Advisory smoke-grep for direct `MutableState` writes inside composable bodies (heuristic).
Hook.Expected: Advisory only; false positives are frequent (inside `LaunchedEffect`, callback, or slot lambda). Manually inspect each match — the finding is a violation ONLY when the write executes at composition time.

Hook.Purpose: Advisory smoke-grep for `@Composable` functions whose `Modifier` parameter is not last (or missing when needed).
Hook.Expected: Empty or few advisories; every hit is a signature to fix per `AX_MODIFIER_CHAIN`.

Hook.Purpose: Android Lint on debug variant — catches `ComposableNaming`, `ComposableLambdaParameterNaming`, `RememberInComposition`, `ProduceStateDoesNotAssignValue`, and other Compose-specific lints.
Hook.Expected: Exit 0. Compose lint issues elevated to error via `lint.xml`.

ComposeCodingRules.RewardCriteria:
✅ Every reusable composable is stateless (`value` + `onValueChange`); stateful wrapper exists only as a convenience. ✅ `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` is the LAST parameter of every UI-emitting composable. ✅ Every `mutableStateOf(...)` wrapped in `remember { ... }`; `by remember { mutableStateOf(x) }` used at declaration sites. ✅ `rememberSaveable` used for UI state that must survive process death (form inputs, expansion flags). ✅ Side effects entered via the correct API (`LaunchedEffect` for keyed suspend, `DisposableEffect` for subscribe/unsubscribe, `rememberCoroutineScope` for click-launched coroutines, `produceState` for one-shot suspend → state). ✅ Composable body free of I/O, blocking calls, direct `Dispatchers.*` `withContext`, direct scope launches. ✅ Stability restored on external-list parameters via `ImmutableList` / `@Immutable` holder; recomposition audited via Compose Compiler reports. ✅ `LazyColumn` / `LazyRow` items supply stable domain-id `key`; heterogeneous lists supply `contentType`. ✅ `StateFlow` from ViewModel consumed via `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`; render via `when` on sealed UI state. ✅ `CompositionLocal` used for UI-only cross-cutting concerns (theme, density); domain services enter via `ViewModel` / explicit parameters. ✅ `@Preview` covers every meaningful state axis; previews inject fake dependencies; naming: `Preview_`. ✅ Composable naming: `PascalCase` for UI-emitting; verb-shape (`rememberX`, `animateX`) for value-returning composables. ✅ Compose UI tests prefer semantic queries; `testTag` reserved for cases with no semantics; virtual `mainClock` for animation assertions.
❌ `mutableStateOf` write during composition body (outside a callback / side-effect entry). ❌ `mutableStateOf` without a surrounding `remember`. ❌ Coroutine launched from composition body (not from a user callback via `rememberCoroutineScope` or a `LaunchedEffect`). ❌ Missing `key` on a reorderable `LazyColumn` / `LazyRow`. ❌ Hard-coded `Modifier.padding(...)` / `Modifier.background(...)` on a composable root; `modifier` parameter missing or not last. ❌ Unstable list / map parameter without an `@Immutable` holder or `ImmutableList`. ❌ `CompositionLocal` holding a domain service (repository, use-case). ❌ `@Preview` instantiating real `hiltViewModel()`, `LocalContext.current.getSystemService(...)` with side effects, or firing real network. ❌ I/O, `File.readText`, `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` inside composition body. ❌ `SideEffect` used for anything other than snapshot→non-Compose bridge (no I/O, no coroutine launch). ❌ Composable naming: `Show*` / `Draw*` prefixes; slot parameters named `slot1` / `bodyLambda`.
Cross-linked directives: ● `kotlin-rules` — baseline language rules (transitive parent). KDoc contract, structural anchors, null-safety, immutability, exhaustive `when` on sealed UI state. ● `kotlin-coroutines` — direct parent. All coroutine surfaces used inside Compose side effects (`LaunchedEffect`, `rememberCoroutineScope`, `produceState`, `snapshotFlow`, `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`) inherit its structured-concurrency, dispatcher-injection, and Flow-discipline rules. ● `android-testing` — Compose UI test rule integration; JUnit4/JUnit5 base for `ComposeTestRule`. ● `android-setup` — Compose compiler plugin activation + stability-report configuration in Gradle.
